To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the threshold current of a GaInAsP surface emitting laser is strongly affected by the mirror reflectivity and that an optimum mirror reflectivity exists for a given structure.
the threshold current density of GaInAsP surface emitting laser diode is dependent on the reflectivity of the mirror.

the threshold current of a 1.3-mu m GaInAsp/InP surface- emitting laser was reduced to 4.5mA at 77 K, which indicates that the threshold current density can be reduced to less than 1 kA/cm2 at 77 K by optimizing the reflectivity of the mirror.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the threshold current of surface emitting lasers with different reflectivity of the mirrors.
the threshold current of a GaInAsP-InP surface emitting laser with a Si/Si0/sub 2/ dielectric mirror.
the development of a GaInAsP surface emitting laser with a Si/Si02 mirror and the investigation of its characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the threshold current of surface emitting lasers is a strong function of the mirror reflectivity and that the reflectivity dependence of the threshold current is a function of the active layer thickness.
the threshold current density of surface emitting lasers is determined by the mirror loss and the threshold current can be reduced by increasing the mirror loss.
the threshold current of surface-emitting laser is strongly dependent on the reflectivity of the Si/SiO2 mirror.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a GaInAsP surface-emitting laser that has a low threshold current and high output power at 77 K.
the threshold current density is determined by the mirror loss and the gain.
the reflectivity of the mirror has a significant influence on threshold current of a surface-emitting laser.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the threshold current can be reduced by a factor of 3-4 by using a high-reflectivity mirror.
the threshold current of a surface-emitting laser is very sensitive to the reflectivity of the Si/SiO2 mirror.
the threshold current can be reduced to a very low value by optimizing the mirror structure.
